nodes.label: AIGate Design Spec (2026-09-22)
nodes.rationale: AIGate is a new independent AI gateway with 9router's full capability but zero 9router code; 9router is behavioral source of truth only at development time.

nodes.label: 9router as Behavioral Source of Truth (not a template to port)
nodes.rationale: behavioral.md §FINAL: 'Do not port the old code. Extract its knowledge. Then engineer the new system.' Shipped product must contain zero 9router code, architecture or technical debt.

nodes.label: Hexagonal architecture, granularity = bounded context
nodes.rationale: Granularity is bounded context, not per-endpoint — 154 endpoints collapse to 10 contexts and only 6 ports.

nodes.label: Monorepo layout (apps/server, apps/web, apps/cli, packages/engine, contracts, database, tools)
nodes.rationale: packages/engine sits OUTSIDE NestJS — the provider-protocol domain must not know the framework exists; also lets the engine be tested without booting the server.

nodes.label: Canonical Internal Protocol (CIP)
nodes.rationale: Replaces 9router's OpenAI-pivot. Vendor-neutral intermediate format: ~13 protocol adapters in + N provider adapters out grows linearly, vs 48 translators growing N². Two iron rules: Canonical is a true superset with typed vendorExtensions, and never silently drop — unrepresentable fields throw UnsupportedFeature. These two rules are why AIGate needs no 'direct route' escape hatch.

nodes.label: vendorExtensions — typed carry-through field
nodes.rationale: OpenAI-pivot lost thinking blocks, tool-id mapping and cache_control. If Canonical is not a real superset, AIGate repeats the same defect under a new name.

nodes.label: AIGate domain model (Provider, Credential, RoutingPolicy, AccountLock, …)
nodes.rationale: behavioral.md §9 forbids concepts living as string/object/if-else/magic constant. Example: 9router's modelLock_{model} key string inside a JSON blob becomes the AccountLock entity.

nodes.label: AccountLock entity
nodes.rationale: Replaces the string key modelLock_{model}: accountId, modelId|null (null = whole account), reason: ErrorCode, until: Date.

nodes.label: Port law — a port exists only with a real second implementation or a mandatory I/O fake boundary
nodes.rationale: Otherwise application calls the adapter directly. Settings/apiKey/pricing are plain Drizzle repository classes — adding a GetSettingsUseCase for GET /settings is over-engineering per rules.md item 1.

nodes.label: AIProviderPort
nodes.rationale: Implemented per protocol FAMILY, not per vendor. OpenAI-compatible carries most; kiro/cursor/commandcode/vertex/azure get their own adapters. Interface: execute, stream, getModels, validateCredential.

nodes.label: HttpTransportPort
nodes.rationale: Implementations: relay / proxy / direct / MITM-bypass DNS.

nodes.label: CredentialStorePort
nodes.rationale: DB today, OS keychain tomorrow — the real second implementation justifying the port.

nodes.label: SecretCipherPort
nodes.rationale: Encrypts OAuth tokens and sudo secrets at rest.

nodes.label: ClockPort
nodes.rationale: Quota reset windows and token expiry must be deterministic in test.

nodes.label: EventBusPort
nodes.rationale: Usage SSE broadcast.

nodes.label: Bounded context: identity
nodes.rationale: login, JWT cookie, password, OIDC, SAML, Local Mode.

nodes.label: Bounded context: apikeys
nodes.rationale: issue / validate / revoke API keys.

nodes.label: Bounded context: catalog
nodes.rationale: provider registry, model, capabilities, alias, pricing.

nodes.label: Bounded context: connections
nodes.rationale: multi-account credentials, OAuth flow + refresh, AccountLock.

nodes.label: Bounded context: routing (core)
nodes.rationale: The core context: 8 lanes, CIP, combo, capacity adapter, token saver.

nodes.label: Bounded context: transport
nodes.rationale: proxy pool, relay deploy, outbound proxy, MITM bypass DNS.

nodes.label: Bounded context: usage
nodes.rationale: history/daily, quota tracker, request detail, live SSE.

nodes.label: Bounded context: media
nodes.rationale: 9 media kinds, voice list.

nodes.label: Bounded context: tooling
nodes.rationale: CLI tools writer, skills, console log, tunnel, MITM control, MCP.

nodes.label: Bounded context: settings
nodes.rationale: settings + guard against mass-assignment.

nodes.label: Error taxonomy (8 ErrorCodes)
nodes.rationale: The recoverable table must be explicit domain DATA, not `if (status === 429 || status === 503)` scattered around.

nodes.label: ErrorCode: INVALID_REQUEST
nodes.rationale: Explicitly NOT recoverable: a malformed 400 swept across 4 providers burns money and user time.

nodes.label: Fallback policy — only recoverable errors fall back
nodes.rationale: Explicit policy pipeline CandidateResolver → attempt → classify(error) → recoverable? yes→next candidate / no→return error immediately. Not nested try/catch (behavioral.md §20).

nodes.label: IMPLEMENTATION_ACCIDENT — debt not inherited from 9router
nodes.rationale: behavioral.md §27: 'old code using a global mutable map does not make a global mutable map a business requirement.' Replacements: global._* → NestJS DI singleton; global mutex → provider-keyed mutex; modelLock string → AccountLock entity; sync usage write → buffered writer with cap and drop-oldest counter; parallel token refresh → single-flight per connectionId; magic numbers → named config; proxy LRU → LRU+TTL; bare Promise.all → explicit concurrency limit.

nodes.label: SB-1 — PXPIPE ignores token-saver master opt-out header
nodes.rationale: 9router chatCore.js:287 checks only pxpipeEnabled, so a client sending the token-saver opt-out header is still processed by pxpipe. Expected: opt-out must disable the whole pipeline. Suspected bug — do not reproduce, label and ask.

nodes.label: Decision: do NOT clone 9Remote
nodes.rationale: 9Remote has no backend, no route, no DB — just a button + modal advertising the third-party 9remote.cc. §14 defines parity as 'same USEFUL behavior'; advertising another product is not useful behavior. The genuinely valuable piece is the Tailscale tunnel, which IS cloned.

nodes.label: Mandatory 6-phase feature process (A Discovery → F Parity)
nodes.rationale: behavioral.md §4 forbids jumping straight to code. A Discovery, B Behavior extraction (20 questions §3 + 12 questions §30), C Contract with REFERENCE_BEHAVIOR/SUSPECTED_BUG/IMPLEMENTATION_ACCIDENT labels, D Design, E Implementation, F Parity verification.

nodes.label: Feature Matrix — mandatory 17-column artifact
nodes.rationale: Must cover all 23 feature groups of §5. No feature counts as understood until its full flow is traced.

nodes.label: Definition of Done — 13 items, not self-awarded
nodes.rationale: Missing one item → status != DONE.

nodes.label: Feature group: Remote functionality
nodes.rationale: Ambiguous name — must be split before tracing: 9remote (empty, dropped) vs Tailscale tunnel (real, 7 routes).

nodes.label: Feature group: Translation / language functionality
nodes.rationale: Ambiguous name — in 9router this is TWO things: the format translation engine (/api/translator/*, 6 routes) and UI i18n (/api/locale, 1 route). Trace both.

nodes.label: Parity verification — 3 tiers
nodes.rationale: §24 forbids testing implementation details; §14 says feature parity ≠ code parity. Therefore NO byte-for-byte diff of the upstream request against 9router — that would force code parity at the translator layer. Only tiers 1–2 are blocking gates.

nodes.label: Parity tier 1 — Client contract (PASS/FAIL, the real contract)
nodes.rationale: Compares semantics of the response AIGate returns: event order, concatenated deltas, assembled message, tool_call mapping, token usage, error code.

nodes.label: Parity tier 2 — Vendor acceptance (PASS/FAIL)
nodes.rationale: Does the vendor accept AIGate's upstream request and return the right CLASS of response.

nodes.label: Parity tier 3 — Upstream shape drift (warning only)
nodes.rationale: Semantic diff of upstream requests between AIGate and 9router. Warning only, never blocking — different ≠ wrong.

nodes.label: Recording proxy + 4-part tape
nodes.rationale: Exploits 9router's own outboundProxyUrl feature so not one line of 9router is modified. Each tape holds clientRequest / upstreamRequest / upstreamResponse / clientResponse; replay feeds clientRequest to AIGate and stubs the vendor — no network, no credits, CI-runnable. AIGate runs on a different port so both systems live side by side.

nodes.label: Normalizer + semantic SSE diff (not chunk diff)
nodes.rationale: Freezes timestamp, request-id, nonce, Date header, multipart boundary, header order. Chunk boundaries may legitimately differ, so comparison is on event order/type, concatenated delta string, assembled message, tool_call id mapping and token counts.

nodes.label: capabilities.md — parity coverage denominator
nodes.rationale: Generated from discovery; each tape marks which items it covers (provider adapters, protocol adapters, routes, providers).

nodes.label: Stated limits of tape-based parity
nodes.rationale: Providers needing real credentials can only be taped on a machine holding the key. Tapes freeze vendor behaviour at capture time — a vendor format change leaves old tapes green while production breaks, so periodic recapture is required.

nodes.label: Golden scenario: client cancellation
nodes.rationale: Barely tested in 9router — a place AIGate must be BETTER, not merely equal.

nodes.label: Golden scenario: partial stream failure
nodes.rationale: Barely tested in 9router — a place AIGate must be BETTER, not merely equal.

nodes.label: Milestone M-1 · Discovery
nodes.rationale: Phase A+B for all 23 feature groups, producing the full Feature Matrix and capabilities.md. Not one line of product code. A+B done once system-wide because only a whole-system view reveals overlapping features; C→F is decision-and-build and belongs inside each SP, since doing it early makes it stale before use.

nodes.label: Milestone M1 · Walking skeleton (thin end-to-end slice)
nodes.rationale: Single goal: one streaming POST /v1/chat/completions with a valid API key through ONE provider, passing all 13 golden scenarios. Acceptance gate: parity tiers 1+2 clean.

nodes.label: Milestone M2 · Scale-out (parallel branches)
nodes.rationale: Acceptance gate: parity coverage reaches the agreed threshold across all of capabilities.md.

nodes.label: SPIKE-1 — drizzle-orm/sqlite-proxy on node:sqlite + sql.js
nodes.rationale: Blocks M0. If it fails, the DB fork must be revisited: hand-written raw repositories, or drop sql.js and lose the 'installs without build tools' guarantee.

SP2 — SPIKE-1 + Drizzle schema + 4-tier driver chain + migration runner
SP3 — Parity harness 3 tiers + recording proxy + normalizer + coverage report

SP5 — settings context (read/merge defaults + mass-assignment guard)

SP7 — engine: CIP core, schema registry, capability resolution
SP10 — engine: protocol adapter in/out (OpenAI only)
SP12 — routing: chat lane + Fastify raw streaming, backpressure, cancellation
nodes.rationale: Explicitly the hardest SP of M1 — it is why Fastify was chosen over Express (needs real reply.raw + backpressure).

nodes.label: SP14 — Provider adapters by protocol family (kiro, cursor, commandcode, vertex, azure…)
SP16 — OAuth for 20 providers: flow + single-flight refresh + reactive/proactive
SP17 — Multi-account fallback: fill-first/round-robin/sticky, AccountLock, provider-keyed mutex
SP18 — Full transport: 4 proxy pool types, relay auto-deploy, outbound proxy, MITM-bypass DNS, strictProxy, LRU+TTL
SP19 — Combo: fallback / round-robin / fusion (panel + judge + quorum-grace) + concurrency limit
SP20 — Capacity Adapter: capability pools, reorder, history trimming
SP21 — Token Saver 5 tiers, fail-open end to end, fixes SB-1
SP22 — Remaining 7 lanes: embeddings, image, tts, stt, video, search, fetch

SP25 — tooling: cli-tools, skills, console log, tunnel, MITM, MCP, provider-nodes
Critique of 9router's information architecture
nodes.rationale: Settings has no home (scattered across profile/endpoint/token-saver/combos); no overview screen (/dashboard redirects to endpoint); shipped-but-hidden features (basic-chat, pxpipe, mitm not in nav); internal Debug tools exposed in product nav; 5 of 9 media kinds shown arbitrarily; flat 12-item nav; monolithic pages (endpoint 1310 lines).

nodes.label: New IA — 7 groups organised by user job
nodes.rationale: Overview · Gateway · Providers · Traffic · Network · Integrations · Settings. Three laws: no hidden nav items (a feature is in nav or deleted); dev-only surfaces sit behind the Settings→Developer switch, off by default; all 9 media kinds shown, unconfigured ones disabled with a reason rather than hidden.

nodes.label: Web stack (Vite, TanStack Router/Query/Virtual, RHF+zod, Tailwind+Radix, Recharts, i18next)
Feature-based frontend structure with import boundaries
nodes.rationale: The frontend edition of hexagonal: a feature may not import a feature (lift to shared/ or compose at the route layer, enforced by eslint-plugin-boundaries); a component only rises to shared/ui when ≥2 features genuinely use it. Route components capped at ~200 lines.

nodes.label: Minimal frontend state management
nodes.rationale: Server state stays in TanStack Query with no mirror store; shared state goes in URL search params; local UI state in useState; SSE pushes straight into the Query cache. No global store until a need is proven.

nodes.label: UI performance constraints
nodes.rationale: Virtualize any list that can exceed ~50 rows; every query must carry limit + cursor with no unbounded endpoint; client ring buffer with a hard node cap for SSE; route code-splitting with lazy Recharts/Monaco; 200ms debounce + keepPreviousData; ONE combined request for all 13 CLI tool statuses, not 13.

nodes.label: Screen state conventions (loading, refetch, empty, error, live, destructive, optimistic)
nodes.rationale: Skeletons shaped like real content, never full-page spinners; refetch keeps old data; empty states must say what's missing, why, and offer one action; errors always give a code, a human sentence and a retry; destructive actions require typing the object name; optimistic updates only for cheap reversible toggles — never for relay deploy or CA install.

nodes.label: AuthFlow — declarative, data-driven auth step framework
nodes.rationale: 9router has 12 hand-written auth modals (CursorAuthModal, KiroAuthModal, GitLabAuthModal, IFlowCookieModal, OAuthModal, ManualConfigModal…) — the deepest niche in the whole UI. AIGate collapses them to 7 declarative step kinds (text, oauth-popup, device-code, paste-cookie, import-file, choose-social, confirm); a new provider only declares a step array. This is §14 in its truest form: identical behaviour, far less code.

nodes.label: Routing simulator (decision-tree dry run)
nodes.rationale: The most valuable thing on the Routing screen: 9router offers no way to preview routing. Paste a real request, see the model → candidate → account tree with select/reject reasons. Dry-run, never calls the vendor.

nodes.label: Quota provenance — vendor-reported vs self-derived
nodes.rationale: §21 forbids merely copying 9router's quota UI. Vendor-returned quota and self-inferred quota have different trust levels and must never be blended into one number.

nodes.label: Server-side secret redaction in request details
nodes.rationale: §23: show requestId, traceId, provider, account, model, attempt, latency, TTFT, tokens, fallback reason, final status — but NEVER API key / access token / refresh token. Redaction happens at the server layer, not the client.

nodes.label: Hard constraint: tunnel requires 'Require API key' enabled
nodes.rationale: Opening a tunnel exposes the gateway to the Internet; without an API key that is a wide-open gateway for anyone.

nodes.label: CLI-tool config writes require diff preview + backup
nodes.rationale: Writing to ~/.claude/settings.json is writing into someone's home. 9router backs up but never lets the user preview — AIGate must show the diff and back up before writing.

nodes.label: Overview — /
nodes.rationale: New screen. Answers in 3 seconds: is the system alive, how fast are tokens/money burning, what is broken. One combined GET /overview/summary plus SSE /events/requests. The 'Needs attention' card unifies AccountLock + OAuth expiry + quota, which 9router scatters across three places.

nodes.label: Endpoint & Keys — /gateway/endpoint
nodes.rationale: Endpoint variant tabs (OpenAI/Anthropic/Gemini/Codex): 9router has 5 rewrite paths but shows only one, and client double-prefixing is a frequent support cause. Key shown in full exactly once; masked by default with a 10s reveal.

nodes.label: Routing & Fallback — /gateway/routing
nodes.rationale: The ONLY place that decides where a request goes: combo + fallback + capacity adapter merged, because 9router separates them so nobody can see overall priority order. AccountLock shows a real countdown instead of a bare 'unavailable'.

nodes.label: Token Saver — /gateway/token-saver
nodes.rationale: Pipeline drawn in execution order RTK ▸ Headroom ▸ Caveman ▸ Ponytail ▸ PXPIPE. Each tier reports how often it failed and was skipped — silent fail-open means nobody notices breakage. PXPIPE 'running' means the module is loaded, not that a port is listening.

nodes.label: LLM Providers — /providers, /:id, /new
nodes.rationale: 123 virtualized cards with lazy logos and client-side filtering, 200ms debounce. getEffectiveStatus niche: a connection marked unavailable whose lock expired must display active again with an explanatory tooltip.

nodes.label: Media Providers — /providers/media/:kind, /:kind/:id
nodes.rationale: All 9 kinds as tabs; kinds with no configured provider are dimmed and labelled, not hidden. TTS adds a voice browser with region names via Intl.DisplayNames.

nodes.label: Connections & AuthFlow — /providers/connections
nodes.rationale: Bulk 'test all' must carry an explicit concurrency limit — never Promise.all over the whole table.

nodes.label: Usage — /traffic/usage
nodes.rationale: Charts read the pre-aggregated daily table, never scan the history table. Custom ranges have a length cap; beyond it resolution drops rather than row count rising.

nodes.label: Requests — /traffic/requests, /:id
nodes.rationale: New UI for request-details, which 9router exposes via API but never surfaces. Detail view is a vertical per-attempt timeline; Vendor request/response and Client response tabs only appear in Developer mode.

nodes.label: Console — /traffic/console (dev only)
nodes.rationale: 200-line ring is a hard cap on BOTH sides — server keeps no more, client renders no more. ANSI stripped server-side; dropped-line count shown.

nodes.label: Proxy Pools — /network/proxy-pools
nodes.rationale: 3-step relay auto-deploy wizard (Vercel/Cloudflare/Deno), token masked and never logged, poll to READY with a 120s cap. strictProxy toggle must spell out that disabling it sends traffic direct when the proxy dies, leaking the real IP silently. 'Used by N connections' column blocks deleting a live pool.

nodes.label: MITM — /network/mitm
nodes.rationale: The one screen where terse copy is FORBIDDEN: it installs a root CA into the OS trust store and edits the hosts file — actions that are not easily reversible. Per-button typed confirmation; Windows warns about UAC ahead of time.

nodes.label: Skills — /integrations/skills
nodes.rationale: Static page, no server state.

nodes.label: MCP — /integrations/mcp
nodes.rationale: New screen — 9router has /api/mcp but no UI. Writes must state which tool's file will be modified, with a diff.

nodes.label: Settings — /settings/{general,auth,developer}
nodes.rationale: Secret fields expose only flags (hasPassword, oidcConfigured), never values; password change requires the current password. Side-effecting settings must state 'applies immediately' vs 'needs restart'. Export/Import replaces the dropped ~/.9router importer, in AIGate's own format, with secrets redacted on export.

nodes.label: Auth — /login, /callback
nodes.rationale: Red warning if the default password is still in use; SSO buttons appear once OIDC/SAML is configured; Local Mode skips /login entirely.

nodes.label: Onboarding — /welcome
nodes.rationale: 5 steps: set password (blocks the default from the start) → connect first provider via AuthFlow → create API key → connect a tool → send a test request. Step 5 matters most: onboarding is complete only after ONE genuinely successful request.

nodes.label: U0 — Design system (tokens, Radix primitives, light/dark theme, standard states, a11y baseline)
U1 — Shell (router tree, query client, layout, 7-group sidebar, SSE client, error boundary, i18n)
U8 — Overview
nodes.rationale: Deliberately last: it aggregates every other feature's data, so building it early means building it twice.

nodes.label: U9 — Network: Proxy Pools + Tunnel + MITM
U10 — Integrations: CLI Tools + Skills + MCP
Skill: writing-lean-bounded-code
nodes.rationale: Targets the 'breaks the rule under pressure' failure mode, so the form is prohibition + rationalization table + red flags. Description deliberately does NOT summarise the workflow — writing-skills warns that agents then follow the description and skip the body. Target <450 words with reference files bounded-patterns.md, review-gate.md, db-checklist.md.

nodes.label: Skill: porting-behavior-not-code
nodes.rationale: Named after the core insight, not the project — writing-skills forbids skills for project-local conventions. Iron law: no product code before that feature's Feature Matrix is done, 'No exceptions'. Most valuable section is distinguishing business rule from implementation accident. Reference files: feature-matrix.md, golden-scenarios.md, error-taxonomy.md.

nodes.label: Split: machines block mechanics, skills teach judgement
nodes.rationale: Anything lint can block (unbounded Promise.all, missing timeout, feature→feature imports, domain importing a framework, queries without LIMIT, route files >200 lines, empty catch, secrets in logs, any/as casts, unbounded retry) is pushed to eslint/dependency-cruiser/CI where it cannot be rationalized away. Skills keep only judgement questions.

nodes.label: Iron law: no skill without a failing test first (RED → GREEN → REFACTOR)
nodes.rationale: SP0 is not 'write two markdown files'. RED: run 3+ pressure scenarios against a subagent WITHOUT the skill and record the rationalizations verbatim. GREEN: write only against recorded rationalizations, nothing for imagined cases. REFACTOR: rerun and close new loopholes. Micro-test the wording 5+ times per variant with a no-guidance control; if 5 runs give 5 different results the wording is too loose — tighten the form, don't add words.

nodes.label: Branding sweep to the bottom of the stack
nodes.rationale: Not just display names: npm package, CLI binary, tray, service name, User-Agent sent to vendors, the MITM root CA's CN, cookie name, schema version marker, config dir ~/.aigate, default port (different from 20128 so it can run beside 9router during tape capture). API key keeps the sk- prefix because clients expect it; the remainder is AIGate's own design.

nodes.label: Open decisions not settled by this spec
nodes.rationale: Parity coverage threshold for M2 (before M2); Basic Chat / Media combo / PXPIPE ship-or-delete (Phase C of each feature); new API key format (SP6); default port and npm/CLI names (SP1); whether drizzle-orm/sqlite-proxy carries node:sqlite + sql.js (SPIKE-1, blocks M0).

nodes.label: Phase model A→F (Discovery, Behavior Extraction, Contract, Design, Implementation, Parity Verification)
§1 Goal — build a NEW AI gateway, 9router is reference only
§2 Core principles — never port, rename, or translate 9router line by line
§5 Feature discovery — inventory every group, do not trust the UI menu
§6 Feature Matrix requirement — nothing is understood until fully traced

§12 Router is its own business engine, not controller logic
§13 Translator/protocol separation — canonical vs vendor formats
§14 Feature parity is not code parity
§15 Code quality — shortest CLEAR implementation, not shortest possible
§16 Do not inherit performance issues; all large workloads bounded
§17 Latency — clean architecture must not add hot-path I/O
§19 Fallback as explicit policy with classified errors
§20 No blind fallback — fallback follows error semantics
§21 Quota must be understood fully, not copied from the UI tracker
§22 Usage fields to trace per request (tokens, cost, latency, fallback attempts)
§23 Observability per request; never log keys, tokens or secrets
§24 Characterization/contract tests prove old ≈ new at contract level

§27 Separate BUSINESS REQUIREMENT from IMPLEMENTATION ACCIDENT
§29 Definition of Done — 13 checklist items, no self-declared DONE

nodes.label: Final principle — 9router says WHAT, never HOW
Rule 1 — Write LEAN code, no over-engineering
Rule 2 — Code must be maintainable, no magic values or hidden side effects
Rule 3 — Optimize performance at design time, not micro-optimization
nodes.source_location: 3. Tối ưu performance ngay từ thiết kế

nodes.label: Rule 4 — Every workload must be BOUNDED
Rule 5 — Low latency: parallelize independent awaits, only when bounded
Rule 6 — Database discipline (N+1, pagination, no query in loop)
Rule 7 — Error handling: never swallow, keep context and stack, bounded retry
Rule 8 — Every resource has an explicit lifecycle
Rule 9 — Concurrency safety (race, double write, idempotency, lock last)
Rule 10 — Cache only with a reason: key, TTL, invalidation, max size
Rule 11 — Review questions beyond "does it run?" (10x/100x traffic, unbounded work)
Rule 12 — Priority order: Correctness → Simplicity → Maintainability → Predictable resources → Latency → Throughput → Optimization
Feature group — MCP (API with no UI, found during spec work)
Provider detail (/providers/:id)
nodes.rationale: Four tabs (Accounts, Models, Config, Activity) keep per-provider concerns separated instead of one long form.

nodes.label: AuthFlow modal (7 step bodies)
nodes.rationale: One shell with seven interchangeable step bodies replaces twelve hand-written per-provider dialogs. Scheduled third — the hardest interaction — while the list/detail pattern is fresh. Step failure returns to the same step rather than restarting the flow.

nodes.label: Request detail (/traffic/requests/:id)
nodes.rationale: Establishes the vertical attempt timeline so multi-account fallback is legible: each node carries provider, account, outcome code and why the router moved on. Absolute prohibition: no credential, key or token appears anywhere on this screen.

nodes.label: Relay deploy wizard (3 steps)
nodes.rationale: Establishes the wizard pattern: named milestones plus elapsed timer plus a 120s ceiling and a scrollable log, so a long deploy never looks hung. Access token field states the token is sent once and never stored.

nodes.label: CLI Tool detail (/integrations/cli-tools/:toolId)
nodes.rationale: Establishes the config-diff pattern: AIGate never writes a user's config file until a before/after diff has been shown and explicitly applied; a manual-instructions block exists for users who would rather it not touch their files.

nodes.label: Settings · General (/settings/general)
nodes.rationale: Every field declares whether it requires a restart or applies immediately, so the user never has to guess why a change did nothing.

nodes.label: Settings · Auth & Access (/settings/auth)
nodes.rationale: OIDC and SAML secret fields never render a value — they show a 'configured' pill and a Replace button, enforcing the no-credential hard rule inside a form that inherently holds secrets.

nodes.label: Settings · Developer (/settings/developer)
nodes.rationale: The developer-mode toggle is the single gate that reveals Console, Translator and raw request tabs; 'Reset all data' sits in a red danger zone behind a type-to-confirm modal.

nodes.label: Login (/login)
nodes.rationale: Lives outside the app shell. A red banner above the card warns when the default password is still in use.

nodes.label: OAuth callback (/callback)
nodes.rationale: The failure variant must name which step of the exchange failed, not just say 'authentication failed'.

nodes.label: Status pill component
nodes.rationale: 20px tall, 11px uppercase, status color at 12% background — low-saturation fill keeps dense tables readable while still carrying status meaning.

nodes.label: Health dot component
nodes.rationale: 8px circle in a status color — the smallest unit of status that fits in a compact card or a 36px table row.

nodes.label: Copy field component
nodes.rationale: Mono value plus ghost copy button, showing 'Copied' for 2s — identifiers exist to be pasted elsewhere, so copying must be one click with visible acknowledgement.

nodes.label: Secret field component
nodes.rationale: Masked by default with a reveal eye, and never renders a stored secret value — it shows a 'configured' pill and a Replace button instead. This is the component-level enforcement of the no-credential hard rule.

nodes.label: Metric card component
nodes.rationale: Large number, sparkline, delta chip versus previous period — a value without a trend and a comparison cannot be judged at a glance.

nodes.label: Warning banner component
nodes.rationale: Amber, or red at maximum severity, full sentences, 2px left border in the status color. Full sentences because the risks it describes (public exposure, trust-store modification, IP leak) cannot be compressed into a label.

nodes.label: Required state: loading skeleton
nodes.rationale: Skeleton shaped like the real content, never a bare spinner — the shape communicates what is coming and prevents layout shift on arrival.

nodes.label: Required state: empty
nodes.rationale: A cause line plus exactly one action button, never an illustration — an empty operations console is a question ('why is nothing here?') that needs an answer and a next step.

nodes.label: Required state: error with retry
nodes.rationale: An error code in mono, a human sentence, and a retry button. Never 'Something went wrong' — the user is a developer who can act on a code.

nodes.label: Density rules (36px rows, 16px card padding, 24px section gap)
nodes.rationale: Compact throughout; prefer a table over a card grid whenever the list can exceed ~20 items, because card grids stop scanning well past that count.

nodes.label: Type scale (12/13/14/16/20/32) and mono for identifiers
nodes.rationale: One sans (Inter) for UI, one mono (JetBrains Mono) for identifiers — model ids, API keys, URLs, log lines, token counts. Table numbers are tabular-figure mono and right-aligned so digits align column-wise.

nodes.label: Status color tokens (green/amber/red/grey)
nodes.rationale: Neutral grey base plus one indigo accent. Status colors carry meaning and are used nowhere else, so color is always information: green healthy/succeeded, amber degraded/nearly exhausted, red failed/exhausted/destructive, grey disabled/unknown. Must work in light and dark; dark surface is near-black, not navy.

nodes.label: Destructive-action rule: type-to-confirm modal
nodes.rationale: The confirm button stays disabled until the typed name matches the object's name — muscle memory cannot produce an accidental destructive click.

nodes.label: Hard rule: no credential ever renders in the UI
nodes.rationale: No credential, API key, cookie, or token value ever renders anywhere in the UI. The dashboard runs locally but is screen-shareable and tunnel-exposable, so rendered secrets leak through screenshots and remote access.

nodes.label: Sidebar navigation contract (identical on every screen)
nodes.source_location: Sidebar navigation — identical on every screen
nodes.rationale: 7 groups, 240px expanded / 56px collapsed, identical everywhere. Console appears only when Developer mode is on; no other item is ever hidden, so navigation never rearranges under the user.

nodes.label: Audit PASS: no credential leaked across 27 HTML exports
nodes.rationale: Scanned all 27 exports for sk-*, ghp_*, JWT eyJ*, AIza*, Bearer tokens and private-key blocks. Exactly two hits, both legitimate: the endpoint-keys create-key drawer (show-once by design) and a masked value on authflow-modals. request-detail — the screen under absolute prohibition — is clean.

nodes.label: Audit FAIL: sidebar not identical across screens
nodes.rationale: Only 1 of 25 in-shell screens (overview) renders all 7 groups plus sub-items; 23 render group labels only. This breaks the shared-shell goal of U1 — using the markup as-is would spawn a separate sidebar per screen. Cheapest fix: adopt overview's sidebar as the single component in U1 and take only content from the other screens.

nodes.label: Audit FAIL: only the happy path was drawn (state rules §10.7)
nodes.source_location: 3 · State rules (§10.7) — FAIL (chỉ vẽ happy path)
nodes.rationale: Loading skeleton on 10/27, empty state on 1/27, error+retry on 4/27. The main table screens (requests, usage, quota, mcp, skills, proxy-pools) have no state variants at all. Fix without regenerating: build <Skeleton>, <EmptyState cause action> and <ErrorState code message onRetry> in U0 and apply across every lane, using deploy-wizard/login-callback as the visual reference for error and connections for skeleton.

nodes.label: Audit finding: MITM CA buttons adjacent, type-to-confirm modal missing
nodes.rationale: Generate CA / Install CA / Remove CA were rendered side by side; the brief requires them spaced apart so they cannot be mis-clicked, and the type-to-confirm modal was not rendered at all. Both must be fixed in code.

nodes.label: Audit finding: Console shown in sidebar regardless of Developer mode
nodes.rationale: overview renders Console by default; the contract is that Console is the one item that appears only when Developer mode is on. Must be hidden when the toggle is off.

nodes.label: Audit finding: settings-auth regenerated as settings-auth-v2
nodes.source_location: 2 · Sidebar đồng nhất / Việc cần làm trước khi vào U0/U1
nodes.rationale: The first pass rendered a completely foreign sidebar (Dashboard · Proxies · Models · Settings · Logs · Docs · Support) and a divergent settings shell, so regeneration was cheaper than patching. v2 has all 7 groups plus sub-items, 'Auth & Access' active, an ERR_AUTH_CREDENTIAL_MISMATCH error block with Retry, and OIDC/SAML using the configured pill plus Replace. Rule: an API is done only when its UI screen is wired in the same SP
nodes.source_location: ## Rule: an API is done only when its screen is wired
nodes.rationale: The SP that adds or changes an API must: wire the screen in apps/web/src/features/<area>/ (api.ts TanStack Query hooks, keep screens.tsx layout, no cross-feature imports); replace fixture data and remove or label controls the API does not back; handle every contract error code with a precise toast/inline message; update API_UI_MAP and the PROGRESS_HANDOFF 'UI wiring' notes; rebuild the graph (/graphify docs --update, build_project_map.py). Prevents a visual preview from being mistaken for live backend integration.

nodes.label: Rule: an SP with no HTTP API records "No UI" in its row
nodes.rationale: So the next agent does not look for a screen (e.g. SP7 packages/engine, SP8 transport).

nodes.label: Failed mutations re-read the server; submit disabled while pending
nodes.rationale: Key mutations refetch on settle, settings toggles refetch on error; the UI never shows an unsaved value and a double click cannot send twice.

nodes.label: UI_READY — visual layout implemented with demo data only
nodes.rationale: UI_READY does not mean API, auth, mutation, validation, SSE or business behavior exists; a demo click is never a completed mutation. Branch is visual UI complete for U0–U11, not M3 functionally complete.

nodes.label: Claude's integration boundary (keep shell/screens markup, add feature api.ts hooks)
nodes.rationale: Keep app/shell.tsx, styles.css, shared/ui.tsx and features/*/screens.tsx as the UI source; do not create a second page/shell for a UI_READY route.

nodes.rationale: A draft for discussion, not an agreed API contract; does not persist or dispatch requests.

nodes.rationale: Catalog is metadata, not 111 working integrations.
